transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:08
Attendees: Elena Morris (Redwood AE), Jamal Rivera (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Oxbridge Head of ML), Marcus Doyle (Oxbridge Cloud Architect), Priya Nair (Oxbridge CTO)

Summary:
Quick scoping session to align on success criteria for a pilot comparing hosted, dedicated and private deployment paths. Discussed workload sizing, benchmark targets, security requirements, and timelines for a 2-week pilot window.

Topics:
- Success criteria and acceptance metrics
- Workload profile and sizing (qps, concurrency, sequence length)
- Benchmarks to run (throughput, p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens)
- Timeline and gating for pilot: data sharing, security review, infra prep

Transcript body:
[00:00] Elena: hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick intros, um i'm elena from redwood, ae on the account. jamal is our se - he does the deep infra and perf stuff.
[00:18] Jamal: hi all, hey, thanks, really excited to dig into the hosting vs dedicated vs private question.
[00:27] Laura: hi, laura chen here, head of ml at oxbridge - we've got production use cases for automated contract summarization and a support triage assistant. mainly short to medium prompts, but occasionally long docs.
[00:45] Marcus: marcus, cloud architect - focusing on networking and cost. we have a hybrid cloud strategy and some data residency constraints in eu-west-1.
[00:54] Priya: priya, cto - i'll be the business sponsor, timeline is Q2 pilot and go/no-go by end of q2.
[01:08] Elena: great, goal for today is to define measurable acceptance criteria and pick what to benchmark. can we start with "what does success look like" for oxbridge?
[01:22] Laura: sure. primary is accuracy and latency. accuracy first - summaries must keep legal clauses intact, we have a human review threshold of under 5% error on key clause extraction. latency target is p95 under 350ms for short prompts, 1.2s for long doc extraction. cost is secondary but needs to be predictable.
[01:45] Jamal: ok that gives us clear metrics: p95 and p99 latencies, throughput at peak, and an end-to-end cost model. also add failure/retry behavior and KV cache hit rate as metrics — we can show token savings with prefix caching.
[02:08] Marcus: from infra side, isolation matters. we may need a VPC or dedicated pool for PCI-type data. encryption in transit and at rest with customer managed keys (KMS) is a must, and audit logs retained for 12 months.
[02:27] Elena: note — we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in private deployments and can enable KMS with Redwood Dedicated via a bring-your-key flow, though implementation differs.
[02:40] Laura: unclear on the tradeoffs — if we do hosted, what's the risk?
[02:48] Jamal: hosted is fastest to spin up, lowest friction: we can run a representative test in a day. tradeoffs: multi-tenant environment, so tenancy isolation is logical not physical; for most workloads that's fine, but for regulated content you may prefer dedicated or private. also note, approximate latency floor is lower on dedicated due to reserved GPUs and reduced noisy neighbor risk.
[03:12] Marcus: can you quantify that? like delta p95 between hosted and dedicated?
[03:18] Jamal: rough ballpark: hosted p95 might be 30-60ms higher than dedicated for short prompts in our benchmarks, but it depends on batch sizes and concurrency. Dedicated yields more consistent tail latency. private on-prem can be similar to dedicated if you provision equal GPUs, but you take on ops overhead.
[03:42] Priya: ops overhead is a big deal. we have a small infra team, so turnkey is attractive. but we also have compliance requirements that push us away from public hosted.
[03:55] Elena: let's map that to acceptance criteria: if hosted meets accuracy and latency targets and the security pack satisfies legal, would oxbridge accept hosted for the pilot?
[04:08] Laura: possibly — but only if audit logs, SSO/SAML, and data retention controls are verified. also need to know how tokens are logged and for how long.
[04:20] Jamal: quick note on telemetry: our console exposes per-request traces, token-level cost, and retention controls. we can mask data in logs before it leaves your VPC for private options; for hosted we have configurable retention windows.
[04:38] Marcus: ok good. now workload sizing: our current traffic is roughly 300 rps steady during peak, with 1k bursts for 5-10 minutes. average sequence length 120 tokens, 95th 450 tokens due to long docs. estimated daily tokens ~40M.
[05:00] Jamal: that's helpful. for pilot we should simulate both steady-state and burst patterns. i recommend two benchmark runs: a throughput run to validate sustained tokens/sec and a tail-latency run simulating concurrent short prompts.
[05:19] Elena: we'll also test KV cache behavior — for the triage assistant the same prefixes appear often so cache hit rate could drop cost 20-40% in some cases.
[05:31] Laura: great. what's the expected timeline to get meaningful numbers?
[05:36] Jamal: for hosted quick-run: 1 full-day to get baseline + cost model. Dedicated vs Private: provisioning for a dedicated pool could take 5-10 business days depending on quota; private on-prem scheduling depends on your sysops but we can run a bench in your environment within 2 weeks if we align dates.
[05:56] Marcus: can we do a hybrid: start hosted for immediate numbers and then run dedicated baseline when capacity is available?
[06:03] Elena: yes that is our recommended path — quick hosted baseline followed by dedicated pilot. we can compare cost/latency and present a decision matrix.
[06:12] Priya: what about data residency? we need EU-only processing for some datasets.
[06:18] Jamal: hosted in our eu-west-1 region is available; we can route requests to regional endpoints. for stricter needs, dedicated in region or private on-prem is the path.
[06:29] Marcus: networking question — if we go dedicated, does traffic need to egress through our cloud provider or through redwood-managed endpoints?
[06:36] Jamal: dedicated pools can be colocated in your VPC (we call that private dedicated) or we can expose a private link; traffic flows over customer-managed peering—no public internet egress required. there are a few setup steps for peering and security groups.
[06:54] Laura: let's talk benchmarks specifics — what metrics do you need from us besides prompts and traffic pattern?
[07:01] Jamal: tokenized prompt samples, expected concurrency envelope, and a list of representative long ops — also an SLO table: acceptable p95/p99, acceptable error types, and redline conditions.
[07:18] Elena: for cost modeling we'll run both cost/token and cost/session estimates. do you have internal thresholds that would sway the decision?
[07:28] Priya: if hosted cost is >30% above dedicated for comparable latency, and requires significant data masking work, we'll likely choose dedicated. If hosted meets latency and security checks, it's preferred for speed to market.
[07:46] Marcus: about quantized models and GPU types — do you have recommended quantization profiles?
[07:51] Jamal: yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization for your workload; for summarization short-seq workloads, int8/4 quantizations often give the best cost/quality tradeoff. we can run quality regressions in the benchmark to ensure no regression on clause extraction.
[08:10] Laura: ok, about acceptance — do we define a go/no-go decision at the end of a two-week pilot?
[08:16] Elena: yes propose 2-week pilot: week 1 baseline (hosted), week 2 dedicated/private bench and ops verification, then decision meeting.
[08:26] Priya: sounds reasonable. timeline check: we need results and contract in place by end of Q2; that gives us runway.
[08:33] Jamal: i'll draft a bench plan with specific workload generators: steady-state 300 rps, burst tests to 1k rps, sequence length distribution (avg 120, p95 450), and a KV cache scenario to measure hit rate and token reduction.
[08:50] Elena: i'll assemble the security pack and compliance summary and send along.
[08:55] Marcus: one more: can we get a sample of request traces and latency breakdowns to show to infra team?
[09:01] Jamal: yes — we can share anonymized traces and the console view.
[09:06] Laura: ok that's great.
[09:10] Elena: recap of next steps: redwood runs hosted bench within 3 business days, oxbridge shares prompts and sample corpus by 3/3, schedule dedicated bench week of 3/14.
[09:25] Priya: agree. any other questions?
[09:29] Marcus: none from me.
[09:32] Laura: nope. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "key vee cache", "VPC" as "VP C", and product names like "Redwood Dedicated" appeared as "Redwood Dedicate" in one segment. Natural speech present: filler words and interruptions were left in for authenticity.
